title: The Successful Failure
subtitle: How three astronauts turned a doomed Moon mission into NASA's finest hour.
_curationNote: NEW CANDIDATE, replaces the-machine-time-forgot (Antikythera) — 0 facts / 0 categories, fully from-scratch. All 4 candidate topics below are sourced and verified but not yet drafted into approved-facts.csv.
_whyThisCandidate: Antikythera was dropped for low remaining wow-ceiling — its 3 best mysteries-topic angles were already mined, and the only fresh sources found were thin (a ~300-word LEGO-replica piece). A same-session Chernobyl candidate was also dropped, on user judgment, for sitting too close to Pompeii's 'historical disaster' flavor. Apollo 13 was chosen after an extended brainstorm specifically for being a different 'shape' of subject (a single bounded mission, not a place or a disaster) and for having zero prior content in the library, so every fact is genuinely new ground. Framed as a triumph, not a tragedy — everyone survived.
_candidateNewFactTopics: The mission itself — the oxygen-tank explosion, the free-return trajectory slingshot around the Moon, and Lovell manually aligning the ship on Earth's horizon for the final correction burn with no working nav computer (category: space)

The improvised 'mailbox' CO2 scrubber fix — square Command Module filters jury-rigged into round Lunar Module ports using plastic bags, cardboard, and tape, talked through by voice with no way to send a picture (category: engineering)
The Apollo Guidance Computer — less computing power than a modern calculator, its flight software physically hand-woven into copper-wire 'rope memory' by former textile workers (category: technology)
The crew's physical toll — dehydration and near-freezing cabin temperatures gave Fred Haise a real kidney infection, documented in an official NASA health brief (category: medicine)
